title: Exact scalar realization for all admissible condensed coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$. Let $\Lambda$ be any of $A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, regarded as a condensed ring with the discrete topology for $A$ and the $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. In particular the algebraic closure has the continuous-function condensed ring, without imposing that a section land in a finite subextension. Put $R=\Lambda(*)$. For any scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], on its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For an $R$-module $M$ let $\underline M$ be its constant module sheaf and set
$$C_T(M)=B_T\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M,$$
using the canonical constant-scalar map and ordinary module tensor [def-sfb-finite-constant-model-data, def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. Then $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $C_T$ is additive and exact on all $R$-modules: every short exact scalar sequence gives a short exact sequence of $B_T$-module sheaves. These conclusions also hold after restriction to every localized site over an object $U$ of $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], with coefficient sheaf $B_T|_U$. For finite $A$ there is a canonical ring identification $B_T\cong\underline A$. For $R=\mathcal O_E$ there is a canonical ring identification
$$B_T\cong\varprojlim_{n\ge1}\underline{R/\pi_E^n},$$
and this actual completed coefficient sheaf is flat over $\underline R$, meaning that tensoring with it preserves all short exact sequences of $\underline R$-module sheaves. For $R=\mathbf Z_\ell$ the same assertion holds with $\pi_E=\ell$.

proof.text: For every admissible domain scalar use the existing constant-to-continuous flatness theorem for PIDs. Fields are PIDs, the standard integer ring is a PID by ULift transport, and finite-extension integer rings are PIDs by the DVR theorem. Finite rings are Noetherian, and PID scalars are Noetherian.

proof.text: On the profinite point, finite discrete functions are locally constant on their clopen fibres. A finite jointly-surjective fibre family makes the constant-functions map locally surjective; its local injectivity follows by evaluation on nonempty objects, with the empty cover for the empty object. Sheafification gives an isomorphism of the canonical scalar map, hence its scalar extension is an equivalence. This includes the zero ring and needs no annihilating-exponent hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 093J, 093M; PID flatness and normalized integral coefficient comparison as recorded in the cited nodes.

proof.text: Compose the scalar-module embedding with exact constant abelian sheafification, exact scalar extension on the point, and the exact inverse image from the point. Reflection by the underlying abelian-sheaf functors proves preservation of finite limits and colimits. Preservation of finite colimits implies additivity. The section-module equivalence and overFunctor preserve finite limits and colimits; the latter is checked by its underlying slice inverse image. This proves every ScalarAssertions clause without a separate identification of slice schemes.

source.place: Tags 093J, 093M; PID flatness and normalized integral coefficient comparison as recorded in the cited nodes.

proof.text: Apply the compact principal-adic coefficient identification to ULift Z_l and to O_E with each chosen generator of its maximal ideal. For Z_l, quotient equivalences with ZMod(l^(n+1)) prove finiteness and the p-adic norm ideal-membership criterion proves the quotient-fibre neighbourhood basis. For O_E, transport the existing spectral topology to the recorded absolute-value topology; compactness follows from the profinite-tower theorem, and replace the chosen uniformizer ideal by the equal ideal generated by the specified pi in the existing coset basis and finite-quotient results.

source.place: Tags 093J, 093M; PID flatness and normalized integral coefficient comparison as recorded in the cited nodes.

proof.text: Reconstruct the pulled-back constant coefficient ring and the canonical scalar map sectionwise. The constantSchemeIso induces an isomorphism i from the actual constant ring sheaf; composing i with the reconstructed scalar map is the canonical constant-ring map c. The completed identification intertwines c and all quotient maps. Apply flat_presented_completion to obtain flatness over constants. Transfer its local finite-relation factorizations across i using its inverse. The sectionModuleComapIso and sectionModuleRegularIso identify every scalar action. This gives flatness of the internal restricted regular module, so extendForgetTensorIso and reflection by the exact forgetful functor give exact extension of scalars on all sheaf modules.

source.place: Tags 093J, 093M; PID flatness and normalized integral coefficient comparison as recorded in the cited nodes.

proof.text: Localize the equational criterion itself: a relation on the slice over U is the same relation on its underlying site object. Transfer its covering sieve along Sieve.overEquiv and retain the same coefficient matrix and generators. This proves the stronger IsFlatOnSite assertion on every slice. Assemble finite, completed integral, and continuous field cases into the unchanged theorem.

lean.note: All six cases use the existing continuous scalar model functor. Clause-packaging helpers retain the actual pulled-back ring, constant scalar map, normalized positive quotient limit, full sheaf-module flatness and localized restrictions. Standard scalar rings are transported by ULift with their induced topology; finite extension rings use the recorded spectral topology. The algebraic-closure case uses all continuous functions, not the extra finite-subextension-valued alternative in the broad admissibility predicate.
